articleTitle: AI-Generated Brain Scans for Synthetic Healthcare Data
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool in generating synthetic health care data, with AI-generated brain scans becoming a pivotal focus in neuroimaging research. This paper explores the current methodologies, applications, and challenges in generating brain scan data synthetically using AI. We discuss how synthetic data can augment clinical datasets, address privacy concerns, and enhance model training for machine learning applications in healthcare. Additionally, we examine the ethical and technical challenges in ensuring data reliability and offer future perspectives on integrating AI-generated synthetic data in health care.

articleTitle: Refreshing Idea on Fourier Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The “theoretical limit of time-frequency resolution in Fourier analysis” is thought to originate in certain mathematical and/or physical limitations. This, however, is not true. The actual origin arises from the numerical (technical) method deployed to reduce computation time. In addition, there is a gap between the theoretical equation for Fourier analysis and its numerical implementation. Knowing the facts brings us practical benefits. In this case, these related to boundary conditions, and complex integrals. For example, replacing a Fourier integral with a complex integral brings a hybrid method for the Laplace and Fourier transforms, and reveals another perspective on time-frequency analysis. We present such a perspective here with a simple demonstrative analysis.

articleTitle: Exploring Virtual Reality as a Medium for Cognitive Behavioral Treatment
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) technology has revolutionized therapeutic interventions by providing immersive, interactive environments that enhance traditional methods. This paper explores the application of VR as a medium for delivering Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), focusing on its potential to improve engagement, accessibility, and treatment outcomes for various mental health conditions, including anxiety, phobias, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). By creating controlled and realistic simulations, VR facilitates exposure therapy, cognitive restructuring, and behavioral activation in ways traditional approaches cannot match. Comparative analysis highlights the benefits of VR-CBT, such as increased patient immersion and adaptability, against challenges like cost and accessibility. Results from clinical studies indicate significant reductions in symptoms and high patient satisfaction rates. Through case studies, data visualizations, and theoretical discussions, this paper presents VR-CBT as a transformative approach to mental health treatment, paving the way for innovative, scalable therapeutic solutions. Future directions include integrating artificial intelligence and enhancing cost efficiency to expand accessibility.

articleTitle: A Novel Power-Gating 8T SRAM Cell with Improved Standby and Operational Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking static random-access memory (SRAM) cell, termed the Power-Gated 8T (PG8T). The innovative design integrates a read-decoupled access buffer and power-gating transistors, collaboratively enhancing the reliability of data read and write operations. A standout feature of the PG8T SRAM cell is its ability to operate efficiently at an ultra-low voltage of 0.32V. Our proposed PG8T SRAM design provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of design metrics across various SRAM architectures, including 9T, 8T, and PG9T SRAM cells. Through detailed simulations, key design parameters—such as hold power, write power, read power, RSNM, read delay and write delay—are meticulously evaluated and summarized. The results demonstrate that the our PG8T SRAM cell significantly outperforms as compared to traditional SRAM cells in terms of power efficiency, achieving substantial reductions in hold power, and write power, often by several orders of magnitude. Higher RSNM value of simulated result of PG8T as compared to other SRAM cell showing better stability and lower read/write delay showing fast performance. These findings underscore the potential of energy-efficient SRAM configurations for low-power applications, paving the way for advancements in sustainable electronic systems.

articleTitle: Smooth Transition MMPC for High-Frequency Attitude Control in Quadrotor UAVs
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study offers a new multi-model predictive control (MMPC) framework for quadrotor attitude regulation that performs like nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) while being computationally efficient like linear model predictive control. NMPC regulates well, but its processing requirements make it unsuitable for high-refresh-rate applications like attitude control. While computationally efficient, LMPC lacks stability and performance in nonlinear dynamics. The proposed MMPC approach uses linear models for quadrotor attitude dynamics and a predictive controller switching mechanism for smooth flight state adaption. To mitigate the “chattering effect” associated with traditional multi-model methodologies—marked by elevated frequency noise in brushless DC motor performance, considerable peak overshoots, and possible actuator malfunction—our solution implements a smooth-switching mechanism known as adaptive gain scheduling. This modification reduces excessive variations in control input, hence improving stability and prolonging actuator lifespan. Comparative assessments reveal that MMPC attains NMPC-Ievel efficacy while maintaining computational efficiency akin to LMPC, outpacing alternative control methodologies such as incremental nonlinear dynamic inversion, sliding mode control, and conventional LMPC and NMPC.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Multiscale Convolutional Neural Network and Advanced Deep Learning Models for Land Cover Classification Using Hyperspectral Imagery
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSI) provide detailed spectral information, making them invaluable for numerous applications. The current study proposes a multiscale 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for extracting land cover from Chikusei hyperspectral data. The proposed architecture consists of three parallel convolutional channels, each employing different kernel sizes to extract features across various spatial resolutions. The performance of this model was compared to other deep learning models, including Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), 1D-CNNs, and 3D-CNNs. Results showed that the multiscale 3D-CNN achieved an overall accuracy of 97.73% an average accuracy of 97.54%, and Kappa coefficient of 97.00, indicating excellent agreement between predicted and actual land cover classes. The multiscale 3D-CNN model demonstrated superior computational efficiency and accuracy compared to the evaluated deep learning models.

articleTitle: Review Paper on Centroiding Algorithm for Lunar Navigation
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This paper reviews on potential algorithms for navigation on the moon's surface, focusing on centroiding algorithms in star sensors or trackers. Accurate positioning is crucial for lunar missions since there's no Global Positioning System (GPS), and navigation depends on pre-installed maps and sensors like Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) and star trackers. Star sensors or trackers are ideal for these missions due to their high accuracy. However, the moon's environment adds challenges, like interference from bright reflections and noise from radiation. This paper reviews different star-sensing methods, comparing CMOS and CCD sensors, and assesses their algorithms for their effectiveness in lunar mission. The research gap which are the strengths and weaknesses of these methods were discussed and identify areas for improvement. By addressing these gaps, this study aims to contribute to the development of more robust and accurate centroiding algorithms, advancing lunar navigation technologies for future exploration missions.

articleTitle: Smart Poultry Farming 4.0: Leveraging IoT for Climate Control and Productivity
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies into agriculture has transformed traditional farming into a data-driven, efficient, and sustainable practice, with poultry farming emerging as a significant beneficiary of this technological shift. This paper explores the application of IoT sensors in smart poultry farming, focusing on their role in optimizing productivity, improving animal welfare, and enhancing sustainability. Key IoT innovations on environmental monitoring, automated feed systems, and health tracking sensors, are discussed in the context of precision farming. Through a review of existing literature and analysis of case studies, this paper highlights the measurable benefits of IoT adoption in poultry farming, including increased efficiency, reduced resource wastage, and improved cost-effectiveness. Comparisons between traditional and IoT-enabled poultry farms illustrate significant advancements in productivity and sustainability. However, the study also identifies challenges such as high initial costs, technical barriers, and data security concerns, providing recommendations to address these issues. This paper concludes that IoT-enabled poultry precision farming represents a pivotal step toward a more sustainable and technologically advanced agricultural sector, offering scalable solutions for global food security challenges.

articleTitle: A Simheuristic Approach Cooperating Skill Optimization Algorithm with Ordinal Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The constrained discrete optimization problems (CDOP) have a stochastic objective function and deterministic inequality constraints. The CDOP is NP-hard due to the large and exponentially growing solution space. The ordinal optimization framework is treated as a recognized framework for resolving NP-hard problems. A simheuristic approach cooperating skill optimization algorithm with ordinal optimization is developed to solve this CDOP in a short time. The simheuristic approach comprises two levels. The skill optimization algorithm is used to construct a differentiated subset with a cursory estimate at the first level. Then, the ranking and selection method is used to find a superior solution from differentiated subsets in the second level. Finally, the approach is applied to the multiple-item inventory system's stock level optimization problem. A real-life example with 5 potential customers and 3 products is used to test the performance. Simulation results reveal that the simheuristic approach can obtain stable and excellent results on the CDOP.

articleTitle: Joule Heating of a 4D-Printed Beak-Like Origami Gripper
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study explores the design, fabrication, and performance evaluation of a four-dimensional (4D)-printed soft origami gripper. The gripper's design features a flat plate with folding panels that form a bioinspired beak-like three-dimensional structure capable of gripping delicate objects of various sizes and shapes. The gripper tips are connected to slot holders designed to clamp the 4D-printed actuators. Polylactic acid (PLA) is used for the gripper and holders, while the actuator is fabricated from a conductive material, which is carbon black/PLA. The gripper and actuator are fabricated using fused deposition modeling with distinct printing parameters. Activation of the actuator and gripper is achieved through Joule heating using a direct current power supply delivering 36 m W. Two actuator configurations, with raster angles of 0°/0° and 90°/0° for passive and active layers, are tested. The actuator with a 0°/0° raster angle shows superior performance, resulting in a tips' displacement of 10.13 rnm, compared to 9.59 mm for the 90°/0° configuration. The findings demonstrate the gripper's capability to securely handle objects without altering their temperature, making it suitable for applications requiring the manipulation of temperature-sensitive items. This gripper design shows great potential to be used in biomedicine, food processing, and robotics.

articleTitle: Manipulations of Organisms and Ecosystems in Artificial Life
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Life on Earth exhibits intricate levels of organization, from molecular interactions to ecosystems, each level manifesting emergent properties distinct from its predecessors. While prior research delves into understanding life's complexities, recent endeavors focus on simulating life through artificial means. Cellular Automata (CA) stand as a dominant tool in silico research [1], offering insights into fundamental life principles. However, existing models often lack considerations for thermodynamic laws and fail to emulate real-life physiological processes.

articleTitle: The Conductivity and the Depolarization Factor of a Spheroid based on its Polarization Tensor and Volume
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The polarization tensor can be used to describe an object presented in an electric field. This is useful in getting accurate image about the object with electrical imaging device or increasing the likelihood of detecting the object with metal detector. Given the first order polarization tensor and the volume of a spheroid, some properties of the spheroid, such as its conductivity and depolarization factor, have not yet been investigated. Thus, this study aims to propose a method to determine the conductivity and depolarization factor of the spheroid, based on its first order polarization tensor and volume. In order to achieve this, the system of nonlinear equations is first derived based on the given first order polarization tensor, before being solved by the Newton's method. Numerical examples are then provided to demonstrate and justify the proposed algorithm. The findings show that the error for the computed conductivity and depolarization factor is small, suggesting that the proposed algorithm is reliable. In addition, the relationship between the spheroid's volume and conductivity is also discussed. The results illustrate an inverse relationship between the conductivity and depolarization factor when considering a positive definite first order polarization tensor. In contrast, for a negative definite first order polarization tensor, the findings reveal a positive correlation between spheroid's conductivity and its volume. The results obtained can then be used to characterize the spheroid based on its first order polarization tensor and also its volume. This provides additional information about the spheroid, which may contribute to the improvement of future techniques in electrical imaging and metal detection.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Volume and the Surface Area of a Charcoal Kiln based on the Paraboloid and the Terrestrial Laser Scanning
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Charcoal kilns are one of the most important assets in Kubang Badak, Langkawi Island. They can be utilized by the Langkawi Development Authority (LADA) to help maintain the UNESCO Global Geopark status that Langkawi Island has held since 2007. However, the charcoal kilns have deteriorated, and only a partial section of their original construction remains. If LADA wishes to reconstruct the complete form any of the kilns, LADA firstly needs to understand the original form of the kilns before any reconstruction planning can be undertaken. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to apply surveying technology called as the terrestrial laser scanning (TLS) and a few terminologies in multivariable calculus to depict the complete shape of one of the charcoal kilns. The data collected from the TLS will be further processed before the paraboloid is used to model the complete shape of the kiln. After that, numerical examples on using the model in estimating the volume and the surface area will be given.

articleTitle: Exhaustive Feature Selection Using Wrapper method for Artery-Vein Classification in Retinal Fundus Image
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Retinal imaging plays a crucial role in diagnosing ocular and systemic disorders by analyzing abnormalities in retinal blood vessels. Numerous diagnostic parameters, such as vascular caliber, centerline pixels, vessel bifurcation, arteriolar constriction, and color reflections, have been explored using machine learning and deep learning approaches for artery-vein classification. While these methods have demonstrated high-performance outcomes, limited research has investigated alternative approaches to identify optimal features for artery-vein classification. This study addresses this gap by evaluating nine color features using a wrapper method across three benchmark datasets: DRIVE, HRF, and VICA VR. The DRIVE dataset achieved the best classification performance, with an Area Under the Curve of 91.49%, accuracy of 83.10%, sensitivity of 84.68%, and specificity of 81.47%. Among the features studied, the Chrominance-Blue (Cb) and Chrominance-Red (Cr) components emerged as the most influential. These findings underscore the critical role of color features in enhancing artery-vein classification. They provide a foundation for further research into feature optimization, potentially improving diagnostic tools for retinal and systematic diseases.

articleTitle: The Role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Interior Architecture Design: Thematic Review
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This thematic review paper delves into the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the field of interior architecture design. The integration of AI technologies into interior architecture is reshaping the way spaces are conceived, designed, and utilized, offering creativity and efficiency. Current research revealed that there is still a lack of review papers exploring the patterns and trends in the use of AI in interior architecture. Therefore, this thematic review (TR) aims to discuss the current use of AI applied in interior architecture by synthesizing the literature from 2020 to 2024 using ATLAS.ti 23. A keyword search, followed by a filter using inclusion criteria from SCOPUS and Emerald databases, identified 30 peer-reviewed journal articles which then were clustered into several themes _1) Design aesthetics and methodology, 2) Innovative material design, 3) Eco-Quality design, and 4) Intelligent system design. The results of this study will offer an overview of the need for a new method of designing interior space, and practical strategies for integrating AI in the interior. This review also serves as a valuable resource for interior architects and designers, seeking into the potential of AI in creating intelligent, and user-centered spaces.

articleTitle: Input Delay Compensation via Barrier Lyapunov and Fuzzy Padé Approximation for Precise Trajectory Tracking for Quadrotor UAVs
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This paper introduces a robust control strategy that accommodates input delay, a factor that is often overlooked yet crucial in real-world UAV applications, to resolve the critical position control challenge for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). To guarantee trajectory accuracy and preserve error boundaries, a Barrier Lyapunov Function (BLF) is implemented, which reinforces system stability by restricting the tracking error to a predetermined range. Moreover, the control framework effectively reduces the impact of the input latency on system performance by utilising an intermediate variable and a Fuzzy Padé approximation method. The control method that has been developed allows for the precise tracking of UAVs' trajectory. The approach is validated by the simulation results, which emphasise its suitability for sustainable and mission-critical operations.

articleTitle: Autonomous Truck Platooning with Vehicle-to-Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Autonomous truck platooning in transportation industry benefit from fuel economy and reduced fossil fuel emissions. Platoon use cooperative vehicle-to-vehicle communications between truck leader and followers. Inertia navigation system and basic safety message communications enable safe platoon operation. Platoon autonomous control system ensure followers follow leader with safe intervehicle spacings and stay within the boundaries of high curvature lane.

articleTitle: Photoplethysmogram (PPG) Signal Analysis for the Heart Rate Estimation Using Shannon Entropy
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: a non-invasive optical technique called photo plethysmography (PPG) monitors variations in blood volume in peripheral tissues. It is frequently utilized in wearable technology and healthcare to track vital indications like heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, and vascular function. PPG measures the amount of light that is reflected or transmitted by the tissues by shining light into the skin. The variations in blood volume brought on by the cardiac cycle are what affect how much light is reflected or transmitted. It can be utilized in healthcare settings for early detection of cardiovascular diseases, monitoring of patient vital signs, and assessment of stress levels. Moreover, it can be integrated into wearable devices, enabling continuous HR monitoring in real-time for fitness tracking and personal well-being management.

articleTitle: Theoretical and Computational Study of Nonlinear Series Expansion for Nonlinear System Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This article asks the question “Does a given nonlinear time series is generated by a unique nonlinear differential equation?” providing negative answer. We show that a given nonlinear time series is generated by a nonlinear differential equation with an infinite number of parameters, and each set of parameters has its own mathematical characteristics (a set of eigenvalues), corresponding to the identity (spectrogram) of the system. That is, we cannot identify the hidden nonlinear equation from the given time series. We show such situations in several ways. As a separate endeavor, we also investigate computational methods in nonlinear analysis, which allows us to obtain a single spectrogram from a given nonlinear time series. We here try both theoretical and computational approaches to a nonlinear system, to find which spectrogram is numerically chosen among an infinite number of theoretical spectrograms.

articleTitle: Control-Enhanced Thrust-Vectoring Rockets: Comparative Insights from PID and FOPID Control
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Thrust vectoring control systems are important given precision trajectory adjustment and increased maneuverability for aerospace applications. This paper compares the performance of the Proportional-Integral-Derivative and Fractional-Order PID controller over a dynamic thrust vectoring rocket system. A tested dynamic model, considering the flat Earth assumption, has considered all the major complexities: nozzle oscillation, thrust inconsistencies, and variation of mass moments of inertia. Similarly, extensive simulations demonstrate that the FOPID control outperforms conventional PID control instability, disturbance adaptability, and performance. These results confirm the potential of FOPID toward enhancing the control precision of thrust vectoring and thus set a background for subsequent research on hybrid and AI-based adaptive control methodologies for use in advanced aerospace missions. The results add weight to the understanding of robust control design, hence giving insights into their applications where high precision is needed, as in space explorations.

articleTitle: Optimizing TAN Concentration Prediction in Various Anaerobic Digestion Systems: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Monitoring Total Ammonia Nitrogen (TAN) is critical for the stability and effectiveness of anaerobic digestion systems. This study concentrates on predicting TAN concentration in AD systems employing multiple machine learning models with a dataset of 2447 units covering various AD operating conditions with various OLR and temperature ranges. Four models were developed and optimized: the Support Vector Machine (SVM) Regressor, Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The ELM model outperformed other models, with a R2 of 0.93 and RMSE of 0.24 on test data. The results demonstrate the significance of non-linear models such as ELM and LSTM in capturing complex patterns in data, as well as the importance of including various AD reactor settings to improve model resilience and generalization.

articleTitle: Improve Black Ice Image Detection for Road Safety
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: A tiny amount of Black Ice that mixtures in into the road's surface is frequently clear or virtually undetectable. In order to detect the existence of black ice on roads, a variety of sensors, algorithms, and methods are used. Black ice detection is essential, particularly for car navigational systems and safety on the roads. The purpose of the research is to propose black ice detection method based on a combination of global and local texture features, such as grey level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP), to capture both overall patterns and fine details. The proposed method is divided into four phases: Image preprocessing comes first, followed by texture feature extraction techniques like GLCM and LBP. Use the relief approach to choose the best feature. Two classifiers, linear discriminant analysis (LDA) and DT, are used to distinguish between images with and without black ice. There isn't a large collection of black ice images that can be used for this research. Consequently, the black ice image data required for the training was obtained through Google image search. According to the findings of the experiments, the proposed GLCM-LBP-LDA attained an accuracy rate of 95%, surpassing the overall accuracy of the most current techniques now in use.

articleTitle: Quadrotor Precision Landing on Inclined Surfaces Using Adaptive Leg Design with Robust PID and Fractional PID Control
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This work introduces a new system with adaptive landing legs to improve the versatility of quadrotor aerial platforms, facilitating safe take-off and landing on sloping surfaces. The design has a lightweight, symmetric leg construction powered by a single servomotor, reducing weight and streamlining wiring, while ensuring stability and balance in flight. To achieve accurate landings on slopes, essential data—including distance, slope orientation, and surface angle—is collected by a multi-zone Time-of-Flight sensor, which demonstrates resilience to visual distortions and fluctuating lighting conditions, surpassing conventional imaging techniques. Landing manoeuvre control is refined using MATLAB simulations, whereby we implement and compare proportional-integral-derivative (PID) and fractional-order PID controllers, emphasising the superior stability and precision of our control methodology. This design markedly enhances the manoeuvrability of quadrotors in difficult terrains.

articleTitle: Soybean Seed Quality Assessment Classification Using EfficientNet B0 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) Efficientnet B0 model to classify soybean seeds into five groups: broken, immature, intact, skin-damaged, and spotted. To enhance model performance, more than 5,000 photos were preprocessed and enhanced with noise, flipping, and contrast tweaks. An SGDM optimizer with a learning rate of 0.01 and mini batch size was set to 32 and 30 epochs was used for training after the dataset was split into training and testing in a 75:25 ratio. The model's validation accuracy was 93.83 % and its training accuracy was 100%. High classification accuracy was demonstrated by the confusion matrix, especially for undamaged soybeans, which had the highest F1 score of 97.35%. Although the model worked well for all classes, there were a few misclassifications because to similarities with other categories, especially for broken soybeans. The outcomes show how well the CNN model can classify soybeans, which may have applications in evaluating the quality of agriculture.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Housing: A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study examines the academic field of Artificial Intelligence in Housing by examining the publications and indexed documents in Scopus and web of science (WOS) from 2000 to 2024. Consequently, we examined the publishing trends, exemplary articles, and the most engaged participants and funding institutions in the domain of AI and Housing research. A bibliometric analysis was performed to examine the network of co-authorships, keywords, and citations in the domain of AI and Housing research. The Scopus and WOS search resulted in the discovery of 246 related publications on AI and Housing. With an increase from 1 publication to 68 publications within the observed years. Additionally, trends analysis indicated a significant increase of 5,016 in publications between 2000 and 2024. Articles are the most often utilized document type, including 172 of the overall amounts. The most prolific researchers in the field of AI and Housing are Ahmad, Chatterjee, Cho, Lee, Mehmood, Shaheen, Yang, and Zhao. All having published 3 documents each. Additionally, ten institutions have produced the highest number of published documents. The output of the affiliations active in the topic is primarily attributed to the funding, specifically the National Science Foundation, which is the leading funding institution based in the United States and has contributed to 8 publications. An analysis of keyword co-occurrence revealed 4 main study areas that cover the essential tools, theories, methodologies, and socioeconomic and financial aspects of artificial intelligence and Housing. Future research in the field of artificial intelligence and Housing will focus on employing sophisticated machine learning, and neural network algorithms to precisely predict Housing transactions patterns while further enhancing housing market transactions across countries.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Machine Learning Techniques for Prediction of Breast Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The prediction of breast cancer prognosis has been a significant challenge in medical research due to the complex nature of cancer progression and the variability in patient-specific factors. Machine learning techniques have emerged as powerful tools for enhancing prediction accuracy in cancer diagnosis and prognosis. This study evaluates the performance of three widely used machine learning classifiers—Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—in predicting breast cancer outcomes using the Wisconsin Breast Cancer Database. A robust framework was designed to preprocess the dataset, scale features, and assess the classifiers using key evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). The results reveal that all classifiers demonstrated high predictive accuracy, with SVM achieving the highest accuracy of 97.08%, followed by RF and ANN with 96.67%. While RF recorded superior precision (95.40%), SVM outperformed others in recall (97.70%) and F1-score (96.05%), showcasing its ability to balance prediction precision and sensitivity. These findings underscore the potential of machine learning to augment traditional cancer prognosis methods, providing healthcare professionals with data-driven insights for personalized treatment strategies. This research highlights the critical role of machine learning in transforming cancer care and lays the groundwork for future studies focused on hybrid models and real-world implementation.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Multilevel Inverter with Minimized Low-Order Harmonics Using Mantis Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: In this paper, the mantis search algorithm (MSA), is proposed to determine the switching angles for a three-phase (3-ph) eleven-level (11-lvl) cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter (CHBMLI). MSA is applied to the selective harmonic minimization pulse-width modulation (SHMPWM) technique to maintain the desired fundamental harmonic while minimizing undesired low-order harmonics. The performance of the MSA-SHMPWM technique is compared to that of a well-known optimization algorithm, the genetic algorithm (GA). For fair comparison, both GA- and MSA-SHMPWM techniques are implemented in MATLAB with the same population size, maximum number of iterations and maximum number of runs. Furthermore, a 3-ph ll-lvl CHBMLI is modeled using PSIM simulation software to validate the effectiveness of the MSA-SHMPWM technique. The MATLAB analysis results show that the MSA-SHMPWM technique achieves a minimum objective function (OF) values of 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup>, which is lower than the 10–<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> achieved by the GA-SHMPWM technique. This indicates that the MSA-SHMPWM technique determines switching angles with higher accuracy compared to the GA-SHMPWM technique. Additionally, the PSIM simulation results confirm that the switching angles determined by the MSA-SHMPWM technique, when applied to a 3-ph ll-lvl CHBMLI, generate sinusoidal staircase-like output phase and line-to-line voltage waveforms with the desired fundamental voltage and minimized undesired low-order harmonics. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of these voltage waveforms, when the CHBMLI is operated at modulation index of 0.60, are 36.61 % and 7.24 %, respectively.

articleTitle: Data Driven Traffic Density Monitoring: A UAV and ResNet50 Deep Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Urban traffic congestion necessitates innovative monitoring and control solutions. This study leverages UAV footage and deep learning techniques to classify and analyze traffic density levels autonomously. By employing a pre-trained ResN et50 model enhanced with additional layers, the research optimizes traffic density classification using UAV-captured data. A custom dataset of traffic scenarios in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, was developed, incorporating diverse conditions through advanced normalization and data augmentation techniques to improve resilience and robustness. The modified ResN et50 model demonstrated high classification accuracy across varied traffic scenarios, validating its reliability and scalability for real-world applications. Key findings include the superior adaptability of UAV-based monitoring for real-time urban traffic assessment and the enhanced classification precision achieved through model optimization. This research underscores the potential of integrating UAV technology with deep learning to advance urban traffic management and foster more efficient urban planning strategies.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Automated Anterior Commissure Localization in Brain CT Scans for Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study explores the efficacy of reinforcement learning (RL) frameworks in analyzing computed tomography (CT) images, aiming to reduce the reliance on labeled data typically required by supervised learning approaches. RL allows the model to make optimal decisions through interactions with the environment, significantly reducing the time needed for CT slice analysis compared to traditional methods. The study also demonstrates the ability to automate the calculation of anterior commissure length, which could help radiologists speed up the diagnostic process by providing accurate measurements for analysis. This research highlights the potential of RL to accelerate medical image analysis, reduce reliance on labeled data, and enhance diagnostic capabilities through the identification of anatomical markers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Smart Grid Stability Using AI Techniques: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The modern smart grid leverages advanced technologies to enhance electricity distribution's efficiency, reliability, and sustainability, enabling two-way energy and data exchange. This systematic literature review (SLR) explores how artificial intelligence (AI) addresses the challenge of smart grid stability. From 1,181 records identified via Scopus and Web of Science, 41 studies were analyzed in-depth. The SLR evaluates AI techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, hierarchical clustering, and explainable AI across functions like fault detection, stability analysis, energy forecasting, and demand response. Findings reveal AI's role in enhancing grid stability through predictive capabilities and adaptive controls. This study contributes a taxonomy of AI applications, identifies research gaps, and outlines a future research direction. Key challenges include scalability, data privacy, and model interpretability, while opportunities lie in hybrid models, and integration with blockchain and IoT. The study provides actionable insights for researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders.

articleTitle: Burned Forest Areas Mapping Using Semantic Segmentation Networks with Group and Shuffle Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Forests are one of the most important resources in a country. However, the number of forest fires is increasing worldwide, and more than 10 million acres of forest are lost every year. Therefore, it is important to have an effective automated forest management system that can monitor and predict the state of the forests in real time. Hence, remote sensing modality through satellite imaging has been used to monitor the state of the forests such as the affected areas due to the fire incidents. It will be very impractical to manually annotate the burned areas, which is the main driving factor for various development of semantic segmentation models for automated mapping process. This work introduces the group and shuffle embeddings to a symmetric encoder-decoder network to enhance forest fire mapping performance. The main task of these embeddings is to increase the variety of features that represent the burned forest areas, as well as forcing each group of filters to extract diverse sets of features. The proposed model, GaS-Net managed to deliver respectable performance with a mean intersection over union of 0.9664, whereby the embeddings are placed at the third block that produces 32 channels per group with a feature map size of 64 x 64 pixels. The model can be further enhanced by analyzing better configurations of the individual group and shuffling modules. This work provides significant insight to the search and rescue agencies to estimate the loss due to the forest fire disaster.

articleTitle: Design of an Electromagnetic Flywheel-Based Energy Harvester with a Battery Management System (BMS) for the Blind and Visually Impaired IoT-Enabled Assistive Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) has greatly expanded the capabilities of assistive devices for blind and visually impaired people (BVIP). However, the increased power consumption associated with these components can shorten battery life and compromise reliability. To address this, the paper proposes a design that combines an electromagnetic flywheel energy harvester and a specialized battery management system (BMS). Initially, load profiling was performed to assess the energy consumption of various assistive devices, identifying the power demands of their components. An electromagnetic flywheel that generates energy when the pedal is rotated, simultaneously notifying the user through tactile feedback that the device is charging. The system includes a voice-based interface to inform users of battery percentage and device temperature. Additionally, wireless communication via the SIM800L GPRS and NEO-6M GPS modules provides real-time updates on battery status and the user's location. By improving energy efficiency and offering real-time monitoring, the proposed prototype enhances assistive devices' reliability, which ensures secure and dependable mobility for BVIP.

articleTitle: Alternative CusTomade Ordering System Using Aveva Edge
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The concept of Industry 4.0 was originally introduced in Germany in the year of 2011. To demonstrate the feasibility of applying Industry 4.0 to a beverage manufacturing line in Malaysia, a CusTomade Manufacturing Line was developed with the One Manufacturing Individualised Solution (OMIS) manufacturing concept. This manufacturing line relies on the default cloud ordering system for customers to send their customised orders to the manufacturing line. However, the existing cloud ordering system is often not reliable. Hence, when the cloud ordering system is down, the customer will not be able to send their order to the CusTomade Manufacturing Line to manufacture the required customised product. Furthermore, the default cloud ordering system is hosted on a limited free subscription and will become inaccessible once the free usage hours are reached. Consequently, this paper presents an alternative localised CusTomade Graphical User Interface (GUI) ordering system that is developed as a solution to the aforementioned problem encountered in the default ordering System. The developed solution uses the Aveva Edge SCADA software, Node-Red, MySQL Database, VB Scripts and File Transfer Protocol (FTP) for this CusTomade Manufacturing Line. The results show that the developed alternative localised CusTomade GUI ordering system performs more reliable as compared to the existing default ordering system.

articleTitle: Small-Scale Dataset for Machine Learning Based Network Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)

authors.preferredName: Wan Siti Halimatul Munirah Wan Ahmad

abstract: An intrusion detection system (IDS) was introduced to detect various intrusive attempts on the network. Several machine learning (ML) techniques have been incorporated to build robust and intelligent IDS. Researchers are maximizing public intrusion datasets, such as the KDD CUP 99, NSL-KDD and the CICIDS-2018 datasets, to train the ML algorithms. However, public intrusion datasets have large data sizes, which cause a high training time for the ML algorithms. Moreover, public intrusion datasets have high-dimensional input features, thus requiring tedious feature extraction methods. Furthermore, these datasets have an imbalance ratio between normal and attack traffic, which leads to less efficient training supplied to the ML algorithms, resulting in low accuracy. An intrusion dataset that can reduce the training and processing time whilst having a balanced dataset between normal and attack traffic must be proposed to overcome these issues. Hence, a small-scale and robust intrusion dataset is developed in this paper to train the ML classifier. Simulation results show that the proposed dataset improves the accuracy of the ML classifier by 19.15%, 99.26% and 40.48% considering accuracy, recall and F-measure, respectively, compared with the CICIDS-2018 public dataset.

articleTitle: Unifying Prediction and Explanation in Time-Series Transformers via Shapley-Based Pretraining
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose ShapTST, a framework that enables time-series transformers to efficiently generate Shapley-value-based explanations alongside predictions in a single forward pass. Shapley values are widely used to evaluate the contribution of different time-steps and features in a test sample, and are commonly generated through repeatedly inferring on each sample with different parts of information removed. Therefore, it requires expensive inference-time computations that occur at every request for model explanations. In contrast, our framework unifies the explanation and prediction in training through a novel Shapley-based pre-training design, which eliminates the undesirable test-time computation and replaces it with a single-time pre-training. Moreover, this specialized pre-training benefits the prediction performance by making the transformer model more effectively weigh different features and time-steps in the time-series, particularly improving the robustness against data noise that is common to raw time-series data. We experimentally validated our approach on eight public datasets, where our timeseries model achieved competitive results in both classification and regression tasks, while providing Shapley-based explanations similar to those obtained with post-hoc computation. Our work offers an efficient and explainable solution for time-series analysis tasks in the safety-critical applications.

articleTitle: A Color-Based Real-Time Target Detection Using OpenCV for DJI Tello Drone
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The utilization of drones has spread into a variety of fields due to the continuous development progress of their technologies. Their applications across military aviation fields into civilian life, where they are performing various tasks such as disaster management, search and rescue operations, and surveillance. Their applications in those operations are possible with the ability to detect the target of the operations. Hence, object detection gained attention in the research community of drones. One of the methods of object detection is color-based detection. The application of the method is not only limited to drones' technology. However, most of the applied color-based methods are designed with a focus on recognizing and labeling the name of the detected colors, but not to detect and recognize the custom target for tracking purposes in the operations. Thus, a color-based detection method without utilizing any advanced machine learning algorithm is proposed to detect the desired target of a drone's operation. A real-time color-based target detection is developed using the OpenCV library. The proposed method is simulated with a webcam and tested with a DJI Tello camera. The results show the target is successfully detected when tested in the same environment as trained. However, the method is sensitive to light intensity and unable to differentiate the target and other objects with the same color. Hence, several improvements to be made are suggested. In the future, for the applications in the drone's target-following operations, the improved algorithm of the proposed method will be put to comparison with a detection using YOLO.

articleTitle: Vulnerabilities in Government Mobile Applications: Evaluating the Security of Mobile Apps in Indonesia and Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)

authors.preferredName: I Made Ari Dwi Suta Atmaja

abstract: The extensive use of government mobile applications in Indonesia and Malaysia has significantly enhanced the delivery of public services. However, this rapid digital transformation also raises critical security and privacy concerns. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the security features of various government mobile applications in these two countries. this study involves deep examination of 50 publicly available government mobile apps from Indonesia and Malaysia, from Google Play. This research focuses on certificate signing mechanisms, and unprotected component analysis. Based on the findings, several security and privacy vulnerabilities in the analyzed applications. This highlights a potential vulnerability in the signing mechanisms used by government mobile apps. Furthermore, nearly 40% of the apps contain exported components that could serve as a surface for potential malicious activities, increasing the risk of attacks and unauthorized access. Additionally, there is one app utilizing an advertisement library, which is uncommon for official government apps and raises concerns regarding the exposure of user data to third-party advertisers. The findings underscore the importance of addressing security flaws and ensuring robust privacy measures in government mobile applications to safeguard users' personal data and strengthen public trust in digital government services.

articleTitle: Utilizing Thermal Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Technology for Precision Agriculture Monitoring of Temperature Stress in Paddy Fields
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Paddy, a vital staple food crop in various Asian nations, including Malaysia, is critical in ensuring food security. The crop's health and yield are significantly impacted by its reproductive and ripening stages, making it susceptible to environmental stressors. Among these stressors, temperature is a significant abiotic factor that notably influences paddy production outcomes. Malaysia has been grappling with the impacts of the El Niño phenomenon since late 2023, which is expected to persist until mid-2024, leading to higher temperatures in the region. In response to this challenge, the study aims to utilise thermal Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technology to closely monitor and detect instances of temperature stress within paddy fields. This innovative approach has the potential to facilitate more targeted and efficient management strategies to counteract the effects of temperature fluctuations on paddy crops, thereby ensuring sustained production levels in the face of climatic challenges.

articleTitle: Mobile Health Diagnostics for Accommodative Dysfunction: Leveraging Handheld Device Technology for Near Point of Convergence Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Accommodative dysfunction is a common visual disorder affecting the eye's ability to focus on near objects, leading to challenges in daily activities. Traditional diagnostic methods require specialized equipment and professional intervention, often inaccessible in remote or underserved areas, leading to delays in diagnosis and management. This study aims to develop a portable diagnostic tool using advanced embedded systems for Near Point of Convergence (NPC) testing, providing accessible solutions for accommodative dysfunction. The project employed the Agile methodology, which emphasizes flexibility, iterative development, and continuous improvement based on user feedback. A Quantitative research design was used, from 150 participants to assess the application's effectiveness. The application demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 92 %, with a sensitivity of 90% and specificity of 94<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, showing a strong correlation with conventional clinical methods <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{r}=0.87,\ \mathrm{p} < 0.01)$</tex>. The findings highlight the potential of this portable diagnostic tool in improving access to eye care, particularly in underserved regions. By enabling early detection and management, this technology has the potential to significantly enhance global eye health outcomes. The integration of such advanced diagnostic tools into routine practice can democratize access to vision care, alleviate the burden on healthcare systems, and improve the quality of life for those affected by accommodative dysfunction.

articleTitle: AI Based Control System for Electric Vehicles with Predictive Maintenance and Adaptive Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This paper presents the development and implementation of an advanced electric vehicle (EV) intelligent control system which is designed to resolve critical challenges such as battery degradation, limited driving range, and system optimization. This study aims to address these challenges by developing a comprehensive Simulink-based EV simulation model that integrates artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for the Predictive Maintenance System (PMS) and Adaptive Energy Management System (AEMS). PMS ensures early detection of battery degradation by using Neural Networks (NNs) to monitor and predict the battery state of charge (SOC) and State of Health (SOH) with an accuracy exceeding 90%. Meanwhile, the AEMS dynamically optimizes energy distribution through Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) to improve driving range by at least 10%. The results of the simulation demonstrate significant improvements in driving performance and prediction accuracy over multiple driving cycles. This research establishes a robust platform for the advancement of EV control technologies, paving the way for more effective and environmentally friendly transportation systems.

articleTitle: Evaluating Indoor Positioning Accuracy with 4- and 8-Light Emitting Diode Configurations Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Accurate indoor positioning is essential for location-based services in environments where Global Positioning System (GPS) signals are unavailable. This study investigates an Indoor Positioning System (IPS) based on Visible Light Communication (VLC), enhanced with machine learning techniques to improve positioning accuracy. The performance of two Light Emitting Diode (LED) configurations: 4-LED and 8-LED, was evaluated across spatial layouts of 16 m2, 25 m2, and 36 m2, Using Received Signal Strength (RSS) data as input, Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models were tested for positioning accuracy. The results show that the XGBoost model outperformed others, achieving the lowest Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.0199 m, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0150 m, and Mean Positioning Error (MPE) of 0.0237 m in a 16 m2 area with an 8-LED setup. Furthermore, transitioning from a 4-LED to an 8-LED configuration improved RMSE by 48.71 % in 16 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area, highlighting the critical role of increased LED density. These findings demonstrate the potential of integrating machine learning with optimized LED configurations to enhance IPS accuracy in diverse indoor environments.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Exploratory Analysis of Fall Risk Classification in Older Adults
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study investigates the application of machine learning models for classifying fall risk in older adults, with a focus on comparing the performance of two algorithms: Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The results demonstrate that KNN significantly outperformed SVM in classification accuracy, achieving 88.1 %, while SVM recorded a much lower accuracy of 47.6%. The statistical analysis revealed that KNN's higher accuracy is attributed to its ability to handle non-linear relationships between predictors more effectively, particularly when multiple clinical indicators are considered. Permutation feature importance analysis identified the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test and Hand Grip strength (HG) as the most influential factors, whereas the Functional Reach Test (FRT) contributed minimally. These findings suggest that KNN offers a more reliable model for predicting fall risk in clinical settings, enabling healthcare professionals to target interventions more accurately. Further research is recommended to validate these findings and explore additional predictive models for enhanced fall risk assessment in older adults.

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Analysis of IoT-Integrated Wearable Systems for Healthcare: Trends, Collaborations and Research Gaps
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The integration of wearable devices and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies has transformed healthcare, particularly in patient monitoring. While current systems primarily alert healthcare professionals, they often overlook the critical role of family engagement, which is essential for emotional support and timely intervention. This study investigates research trends and gaps in IoT-integrated wearable healthcare systems, focusing on predictive monitoring and family involvement for ventilator patients. Data was collected from Scopus and Web of Science databases, covering publications from the last decade. We conducted both descriptive and bibliometric analyses using tools such as VOSviewer and Bibliometrix to trace research progress over time, identify leading journals, top authors, and influential countries, and analyze keyword co-occurrence to reveal well-researched areas. Additionally, content analysis was applied to pinpoint emerging research hotspots within the last five years. Findings highlight a growing focus on predictive monitoring technologies and IoT solutions in healthcare but reveal a critical void in family-centered remote monitoring frameworks. Few studies effectively integrate family support with real-time patient care, particularly in ventilator management. This analysis emphasizes the need for collaborative platforms connecting patients, families, and healthcare providers through IoT-enabled wearables. Integrating predictive analytics can further optimize emergency response and mitigate limitations of traditional alarm-based systems, which are susceptible to human oversight. This study offers actionable insights for developing holistic, patient-centric solutions in wearable healthcare technologies.

articleTitle: Image Analysis of the Nasal Region for Respiratory Rate Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Respiration health monitoring is vital due to the rising prevalence of an aging population, chronic respiratory diseases, and challenges faced by those in rural and underserved areas. Advancements in telehealth applications have allowed medical professionals to monitor and diagnose patients remotely, offering a more accessible and convenient approach to healthcare. However, one of the main challenges in telehealth is the need for physical examination, falling short in terms of providing real-time physiological data to medical professionals. Hence, this study aims to bridge that gap by developing a vision-based, non-invasive respiratory rate (RR) monitoring system using the MLX90640 thermal camera and providing quantifiable respiratory metrics such as breaths per minute (BPM). Using a thermal camera also minimizes the interference of surroundings, such as brightness, which may hinder analyzing BPM when using a conventional RGB camera. A YOLOv8 model was trained using 1,690 thermal images to classify breathing patterns. The system effectively extracted an oscillating signal, representing the thermal fluctuations of the nasal region during inhalation and exhalation. This is further processed by signal manipulation techniques such as bandpass filtering, Fast Fourier transformation (FFT), and peak detection. Ultimately, the camera system was successfully calibrated to monitor RR, achieving an RMSE score of 1.651 relative to the standard method of manually counting BPM by observing the rise and fall of a patient's chest area.

articleTitle: A Joint Gauss-Seidel and Neumann Series Precoding Scheme for a Downlink Massive MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: In the downlink (DL) of a Time Division Duplex (TDD) massive MIMO system, the effect of multi-user interference is ameliorated efficiently by Zero Forcing (ZF) linear precoding, which may achieve an almost optimal sum-rate performance. However, ZF suffers from a high implementation complexity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(K^{3})$</tex> owing to the inversion of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K\times K$</tex> channel correlation matrix due to its direct inversion method. To lessen this complexity, approximate matrix inversion by the Gauss-Seidel (GS) or Neumann series (NS) methods has been explored extensively. In this paper, the authors propose a joint Gauss-Seidel Neumann series (JGSNS) algorithm that approximates square matrix inversion with faster convergence speed and fewer FLOPs than the Neumann series. The performance of the precoding scheme is evaluated in a DL, TDD massive MIMO system as a function of antenna array size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> and number of simultaneous users K.

articleTitle: A Survey on Swarm Intelligence Algorithms for Optimizing Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This survey provides an exhaustive review of advances in Swarm Intelligence algorithms applied to path planning from the year 2019 to 2024. Swarm Intelligence is a field of investigation that takes its inspiration from the behavior of social animals and has evolved to now incorporate machine learning and sensor fusion to solve pathfinding problems of growing difficulty. The application of SI in dynamic and uncertain environments is still problematic, since the efficiency and adaptability of algorithms change greatly under different conditions of operation. The paper discusses how research in diverse fields like mobile robots, autonomous vehicles, and logistics synthesizes and then evaluates the efficiency, adaptability, and performance of prominent SI algorithms. It highlights the integration of SI with modern technologies like machine learning and sensor fusion, which has demonstrated enlarged capabilities in the navigation of complex and dynamic environments. This paper identifies the research gaps and proposes certain directions for future research, hence acting as a vital resource in applying SI with a view to optimizing path planning in autonomous systems.

articleTitle: SW-LSTM: Strong-Weak Long Short-Term Memory Fusion Network for Forecasting Pandemic Spread
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The pandemic created unparalleled global health challenges, resulting in millions of deaths worldwide, effectively halting the world. Various statistical and machine learning models have been previously deployed to forecast the spread of the pandemic worldwide. Forecasting the spread rate supports pandemic control by guiding the creation of strategies to limit its transmission. Despite significant efforts made to forecast the spread of such infectious diseases in India, efficient forecasting using deep learning systems is still lacking. To overcome this problem, we have proposed a novel, effective, intelligent framework for predicting the course of any infectious diseases using a novel LSTM-based fusion model. The proposed model combines two different LSTM networks, the Strong and Weak LSTM models, to improve time series forecasting accuracy. The model assigns 25 % weight to the strong model and 75% weight to the weak model, leveraging their complementary strengths for better predictions. We have used the COVID-19 India dataset. While our tests focused on COVID-19 India data, the methodology can be readily adapted to other pandemic diseases. We have proposed to accurately estimate the rise of the pandemic cases in the near future by considering various factors like; age, gender, geographical location, etc. A brief comparative study with different time-series deep-learning models is also given. The model's performance is evaluated using mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) on the COVID-19 India dataset and provides comparative results with six state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Quantitative Muscle Spasticity Model in Flexion and Extension Passive Movements
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Stretching is a fundamental physical therapy technique for assessing spasticity through passive flexion and extension movements. The conventional procedure required clinical tools such as the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) to assess the spasticity level of joints according to the extent of muscle resistance, resulting in assessment inconsistencies that could impact the efficacy of the rehabilitation process. There is no evidence to suggest that either passive flexion or extension movements are independently used in measuring muscle spasticity during assessments. This study aims to explore the differentiation between passive flexion and extension movements in measuring muscle spasticity during assessments, as these movements may exhibit distinct characteristics using Mechanomyography (MMG) signals from forearm muscles mapped to MAS levels. The findings demonstrate the need for two distinct models to accurately assess spasticity in both movements. Data were collected from 30 patients with upper limb spasticity, including 29 stroke cases and one with cerebral palsy, all of whom provided informed consent under ethical approval. The dataset included 48 features extracted from ACC-MMG signals along the x, y, and z axes during flexion and extension movements of the biceps and triceps of the limb. Statistical analyses, including linear regression and one-way MANDVA, were conducted to examine the characteristics of MMG signal features for each movement. To improve spasticity detection, Decision Trees (DTs), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Support Vector Machines (SVM) classifiers were applied. The KNN-based classifier attained outstanding results, with an accuracy of 90.12% for flexion and 86.42% for extension, showing flexion as the most effective movement for measuring spasticity.

articleTitle: Cost-Benefit Analysis with Dashboard of Solar Panels for Residential Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study develops an investigation of the economic and practical feasibility of the installation of residential solar panels in Malaysia, with a developed web-based dashboard that could be of help for decision analysis. Given the abundant solar irradiance in Malaysia and its supportive energy policies, the research integrates local consumption data, government incentives, and the cost structure into a cost-benefit analysis framework. This study has presented a dashboard that calculates estimates of energy usage, optimal system sizes, and financial metrics like payback period and ROI, computed with respect to user-specified inputs. The result shows the payback period for the solar installations in the range of 5–7 years, whereas the return on investment is around 55% within a span of ten years. The dashboard bridges the gap between technical feasibility and actionable insight, thereby enabling the homeowners to make an informed choice while standing at par with Malaysia's sustainability and renewable energy goals.

articleTitle: Analytical Characterization of Aquilaria Species Essential Oils Using Advanced Chromatographic Techniques Based on GC-MS and GC-FID
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study provides a comprehensive analysis of essential oils from four Aquilaria species—Aquilaria Beccariana, Aquilaria Malaccensis, Aquilaria Crassna, and Aquilaria Subintegra—using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and gas chromatography-flame ionization detector (GC-FID). A total of 720 samples were analyzed, focusing on six key compounds: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-selinene, dihydro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-agarofuran, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta$</tex>-guaiene, 10-epi-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-eudesmol, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-eudesmol, and pentadecanoic acid. Descriptive statistics and normality assessments, including the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, were performed using SPSS to evaluate the distribution and variability of these compounds. The results reveal significant biochemical differences among the species, with Aquilaria Beccariana showing dominance of dihydro-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-agarofuran and Aquilaria Malaccensis exhibits high concentrations of 10-epi-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex>-eudesmol, indicating distinct metabolic profiles for each species. Normality tests suggest that most compound data approximate normal distributions. These findings provide new insights into the unique biochemical compositions of the Aquilaria species, improving species classification accuracy. The research also has broader implications for agarwood conservation strategies and industrial applications, particularly in the essential oils and fragrance industries.

articleTitle: Adaptive Palmprint ROI Extraction Using Contour-Based Approach with PCA Alignment
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: In the evolving field of palmprint recognition, extracting the region of interest (ROI) accurately is pivotal, especially when dealing with images of varied positions and rotations. Past approaches typically employed a constant size square area, typically at the palm's center, leading to potential inaccuracies due to rotation or misalignment. This paper introduces an improved method for ROI extraction in palmprint images using an enhanced contour-based algorithm with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) alignment. This method successfully adapts to the unique characteristics of each palm, ensuring accurate ROI extraction even with varied hand positioning and rotation. The method was rigorously tested across three different palmprint databases: PolyU, IIT Delhi, and CASIA, demonstrating high accuracy rates of 99.07%, 97.5%, and 98.04% respectively. Even under artificially induced rotation, the method maintained substantial performance on PolyU, IIT Delhi and CASIA database with accuracy rates of 96.7%, 88.26% and 96.32% respectively. The results of this study underscore the potential of this method in advancing palmprint recognition systems, contributing to their applicability in broader contexts and varied conditions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Ensemble Techniques for Prediction of Diabetes
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This study aims to explore hybrid machine learning techniques for the predictive purpose of diabetes disease. The primary objective is to analyze existing supervised machine learning algorithms like K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Naive Bayes (NB), Decision Tree (DT) and so on, that are used for predictive purposes by carrying out extensive research. Through this study, several hybrid machine learning prediction classifiers using supervised techniques and ensemble methods will be studied and evaluated based on their performance matrix of accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score as well. This is to discover which predictive technique is the most suitable for predicting diabetes as well as to evaluate by how much ensemble methods can improve diabetes prediction accuracy. This study utilizes feature selection with Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross Validation (RFECV) to determine the most important features of the dataset, as well as K-Fold Cross Validation to evaluate the performance of all the machine learning techniques used by ensuring that different portions of the dataset is used for training and testing. The results of this study reveal that boosting, by Gradient Boosting (GB), is the best performing ensemble technique at 85.904% accuracy, 70.921 %) precision, 56.840% recall and 58.439% F1-score. For bagging ensemble techniques, Random Forest (RF) had the highest performance at 85.903% accuracy, 71.019% precision, 56.486% recall and 57.939% F1-score. On the other hand, for stacking ensemble techniques, Decision Tree (DT) + Support Vector Machine (SVM) proved to be the highest performing combination with an accuracy of 85.870%, precision of 70.585%, recall of 57.524% and F1-score of 59.358%. For the base supervised techniques itself, K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) performed almost as well as GB, with the same accuracy as GB (85.904 %), and got a higher precision of 71.050% but had a recall and F1-score that's marginally lower at 56.380% and 57.789% respectively. These findings are significant because, when compared to other existing studies that used the same dataset (Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System – 2015 Survey), the performance accuracy of the hybrid machine learning techniques in this study was higher, providing new insights on possible suitable processes taken in this study that can produce better results with the dataset used. To conclude, based on these outcomes we can say that hybrid machine learning techniques generally perform better when compared to supervised machine learning techniques and have the potential to contribute well towards future implementations in the diagnostic medicine field, paving new possibilities to revolutionize traditional diagnostic practices in order to help with the early intervention of diabetes by predictive methods.

articleTitle: Comparison of Depression Detection Between LLMs and Zero-Shot Learning Using DAD Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Early and accurate detection of depression is critical for improving mental health outcomes. Yet, selecting an appropriate machine learning approach remains challenging due to differences in data availability, annotation costs, and computational resources. Fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) and Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) represent fundamentally distinct paradigms for natural language understanding tasks. Comparing these approaches is crucial because LLMs rely on large, labeled datasets, while ZSL provides a practical alternative in scenarios with limited or no annotated data. Despite their growing application, these methods are often studied in isolation, leaving a gap in understanding their relative advantages and trade-offs. This study addresses this gap by evaluating the performance of a fine-tuned BERT-LLM and a BART-based ZSL model on our custom-made Depression Analysis Dataset (DAD). Our research experiments showed that the fine-tuned BERT-LLM achieved accuracy and F1 scores of 98.94% and 99.24 %, respectively, while the BART-ZSL model attained 76.53% and 81.26%. The findings highlight the suitability of LLMs for high-reliability settings and ZSL for early detection in resource-constrained contexts, providing actionable insights for data scientists and mental health practitioners to design effective and accessible depression detection systems.

articleTitle: ECG Classification Based on Multimodal Feature Extraction and Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Heart health diagnosis plays a vital role in preventing and managing cardiovascular diseases, which remain a leading cause of death globally. Early and precise detection of heart related problems is vital for effective treatment and enhancing patient outcomes. Traditional methods often rely on single-modal data, which can limit diagnostic accuracy.
