In this study, we present a comprehensive approach to heart health analysis by extracting multimodal features derived from Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and training a Deep Learning model. The methodology involves extraction of both time-domain features using Continuous Wavelet Transform: Morlet transform (CWT) and frequency-domain features using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), enabling a thorough examination of the ECG data. These features were then input into a deep neural network model. The model achieved an impressive accuracy of 99.1% in classifying various heart conditions, highlighting its robustness and effectiveness. Notably, the neural network architecture employed is relatively simple, making it feasible to deploy on mobile or edge devices. This characteristic ensures that the heart health analysis can be performed in real-time without relying on extensive computational resources, thereby making it practical for widespread, on-device use. This approach not only enhances the accessibility of heart health monitoring but also promotes timely and accurate diagnosis in everyday settings.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Ensemble Approach for Robust Deepfake Detection in Low-Resolution Short Videos
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Deepfake technology—synthetic media that replaces a person's likeness in existing images or videos—has raised significant concerns in politics, security, and the media. Recent advances such as ChatGPT 4.0 have further magnified the potential misuse of these synthetic artifacts, making it increasingly challenging to detect maliciously manipulated short videos. This paper proposes a deepfake detection framework to address challenges in low-resolution, compressed, and short video scenarios. The methodology leverages Haar Cascade for face detection, a Vision Transformer (ViT) for feature extraction, and an ensemble classifier (Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, Logistic Regression) for final data modelling. Our result findings underline how high compression, video distortions, and limited training data affect detection accuracy. Experiments on Celeb-DF (v2) and DeeperForensics-1.0 datasets reveal that our proposed method balances computational efficiency and robust detection, outperforming cutting-edge Convolutional Neural Network-based models (e.g., MesoNet) on selected metrics and data partitions. Subsequently, our findings revealed that the proposed ensemble model achieves high accuracy of 74% in detecting the deepfake content on the Celeb-DF (Version 2) and DeeperForensics-1.0 datasets. By focusing on spatial anomalies and practical constraints such as short video duration, this work contributes to a valuable understanding of these constraints and the scalability of the existing approaches.

articleTitle: Advancing Sustainable Paddy Farming: Utilizing Multispectral Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Technology for Efficient Water Stress Detection and Management
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Paddy is one of the crucial crops in Asia. Due to that factor, the demand has been increasing daily, and research has been reported by Das et al. (2022) that the paddy will be in demand and will increase by 50% in 2050. Paddy progresses through different growth stages: vegetation, reproductive, and ripening. The reproductive stage is particularly vital for its development. However, the growth and yield of paddy are significantly affected by water scarcity, especially during the dry season in Perlis from January to April. To tackle this challenge, this research utilizes multispectral unmanned aerial vehicle (UA V) technology to identify water stress levels in paddy fields. Despite its proven effectiveness in agriculture, this innovative technology has not been widely utilized for water stress monitoring. This study aims to utilize the multispectral UAV for water stress detection, improving understanding and managing water resources in paddy farming. This approach can strengthen sustainable paddy production, even in disadvantageous weather conditions. By enhancing water stress detection, we can ensure more efficient water usage in paddy cultivation, thereby contributing to the overall sustainability of this essential agricultural practice.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of IoT-Based Smart Fuel Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The fast growth of the 'Internet of Things' (IoT) has impacted on several sectors, including fuel management. This paper describes the design, fabrication, and implementation of an IoT-based smart fuel monitoring system to improve the effectiveness of using fuel resources while minimizing losses and optimizing processes. A Rasp berry Pi controller with various sensors tracks essential parameters such as fuel level, temperature, pressure, pH, and gas levels. The system also provides for processing and presenting the collected data through a mobile application and a website, making it possible to manage the system further from the users via remote control. The system was tested using two fuel types, Benzene and Diesel, and it was effective in fuel parameters management. Results established that the pressure of Benzene was reasonably constant, and it was about 14.8 psi after reaching equilibrium. In contrast, the pressure returned to 14.7 psi value for Diesel, which was its initial value. The temperature readings were constant throughout the experiment, with the benzene temperature being higher than Diesel. The system also differentiated between pH levels, keeping Benzene at 6.9 while Diesel at around 7. These results prove the capabilities and efficiency of this system in anomaly detection, fuel adulteration, and fuel theft prevention, thus solving modern solutions in fuel management.

articleTitle: Pothole Detection Using UAV with Deep Learning Algorithm for Road Inspection
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Pothole detection is a crucial component of road maintenance, essential for ensuring safety and minimizing vehicle damage. Traditional road inspection methods are often limited by their coverage, labor-intensive nature, and time-consuming processes. This paper presents an innovative approach to pothole detection by utilizing Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in combination with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) algorithm. The primary aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of the CNN algorithm in detecting road potholes. The results indicate a high level of detection confidence, demonstrating that UAVs operating at low altitudes can accurately capture orthophotos for pothole identification. The pothole detection model achieved a precision of 0.437, a recall of 0.800, and a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.740, highlighting its accuracy and reliability. The study concludes that while UAVs integrated with artificial intelligence show promise for effective pothole detection, low-altitude flights present practical challenges due to environmental factors. Despite these limitations, the combination of UAVs and CNNs offers a viable solution for enhancing road inspection efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Performance of ResNet50 in Classifying Artificial Intelligence Generated Arts
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of AI-generated art has sparked debates regarding its authenticity and impact on traditional art. This study evaluates the performance of the ResNet50 deep learning model in classifying images as either AI-generated or non-AI-generated (traditional art). A dataset collected from Kaggle was divided into two categories, and training was conducted using a learning rate of 0.001, a minibatch size of 32, and 20 epochs, with validation occurring every 50 iterations. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 95.45%, with class wise accuracies of 95.82% for Algenerated images and 95.03% for non-AI-generated images. Precision, recall, and F1 scores further confirmed the model's robust performance, with balanced metrics across both classes. The results highlight the effectiveness of ResNet50 in distinguishing between these two forms of art, demonstrating its potential as a tool for addressing controversies related to AI -generated content in art competitions and creative domains. Future research could focus on refining the model's performance by exploring more diverse datasets and advanced architectures. This study contributes to the growing body of research at the intersection of deep learning and creative industries, offering a reliable solution for classifying AI-generated and traditional art.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Classification of Lung Cancer Using Streamlined Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Lung cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, highlighting the importance of accurate and timely diagnosis. Medical imaging, particularly Computed Tomography (CT), plays a pivotal role in lung cancer detection due to its ability to capture high-resolution, cross-sectional views of lung tissue. However, interpreting CT scans manually is prone to inter-operator variability and fatigue. This paper proposes a deep learning approach, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), to classify lung CT images into four categories: normal, adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and large cell carcinoma. Our proposed method relies on streamlined hyperparameters, including batch normalization, dropout, L2 regularization, and data augmentation strategies, to handle imbalanced classes and improve generalization. We conducted experiments using varying image resolutions and train-validation-test splits for model performance evaluation. The best model achieved a 0.96 classification accuracy rate at 192x192 image size with macro average precision, recall, specificity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.96, 0.99 and 0.96, respectively. Our research findings underscore the potential of streamlined CNN architectures to achieve robust model performance comparable to more computationally demanding methods, thus facilitating broader adoption in medical imaging applications. This study also highlights the impact of different image resolutions and parameter choices, offering a practical solution for clinicians and data scientists with limited resources.

articleTitle: Implementation Research of Tiny ML on RISC-V Platform Using Efinix Platform for Real Time Person Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The rapid advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision have revolutionized intelligent security systems, addressing challenges related to cost, efficiency, and scalability. This paper investigates the application of Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) on the RISC-V platform, utilizing the Efinix Ti60 F225 FPGA for real-time person detection. The study aims to harness the energy efficiency, flexibility, and scalability of the RISC-V architecture to develop a cost-effective and sustainable solution for intelligent security applications. The proposed system combines the YOLO model for person detection with TinyML techniques, enabling real-time processing while maintaining an accuracy of 80% for individuals within a 2-meter range. Hardware components, such as the Raspberry Pi Camera Module V2 and Mini DSI Panel, were employed to capture and display real-time imagery. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrated the system's performance advantages, including reduced latency, low power consumption, and minimal bandwidth usage, emphasizing the benefits of deploying AI at the edge. Although challenges such as environmental variability and memory limitations were encountered, the findings highlighted the potential of integrating TinyML with RISC-V platforms for intelligent security applications. The results contributed to the field of edge computing and open-source hardware, presenting a viable approach to energy-efficient and scalable AI solutions. Future research will focus on overcoming hardware constraints, extending the detection range, and incorporating adaptive learning capabilities to enhance system robustness and functionality further.

articleTitle: 4D Printing of a Modular Tweezer-Like Gripper
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: Grippers are end-effectors attached to micromanipulators to perform pick-and-place tasks using their ‘fingers'. The fabrication process of conventional grippers is time-consuming, costly, and involves various materials. On the other hand, four-dimensional (4D) printing is an emerging technology that adds another dimensional aspect to structures that are fabricated using three-dimensional (3D) printing by inducing shape changes through exposure to external stimuli. These 4D-printed structures incorporate the advantages of 3D printing, such as low wastage, fast prototyping, quick production, and customizability. This paper presents a 4D-printed modular tweezer-like gripper fabricated with polylactic acid (PLA) using fused deposition modeling (FDM) printing technique. The modular gripper uses a housing to hold interchangeable actuators for different applications. The actuators of the gripper are designed to be 30 mm long, 5 mm wide, and 0.8 mm thick. These actuators consist of a bilayer structure combining two different levels of pre-induced strain that are controlled using different printing speeds. The deformation of the actuators is achieved through heating in water, which releases the pre-induced strain stored in the printed layers of the actuators. In addition, the relationship between the bending angle of actuators and the FDM printing speed is studied. The deformation performance of the actuators is analyzed using Kinovea software. The standalone actuator with active layers printed at 80 mm/s is found to have a higher bending angle of 87.56˚, while the maximum bending angle of the actuator with active layers printed at 20 mm/s is found to be 23.32˚. As a proof of concept, the gripper is used to grip and hold a clip with a mass of 2214.3 mg, which is around 2.94 times the mass of the gripper. The proposed gripper shows promising performance, making it suitable to be used as an end-effector for robotics applications.

articleTitle: Joule Heating of a 4D-Printed Multi-Material Origami Gripper
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a four-dimensional (4D)-printed soft origami gripper. The gripper's design consists of flat plates that are connected together using hinges that allow folding the structure into a three-dimensional structure. These folding panels form a cage that can grip and enclose objects of different sizes and shapes. The folded structure is attached to holders for the 4D-printed actuator to allow its deformation to close the fingers of the gripper. Fused deposition modeling technique is used to fabricate the structure of the origami gripper and its actuator. The structure of the gripper is printed using a combination of polylactic acid (PLA), conductive PLA (CPLA), and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), while the actuator is completely printed using CPLA. The TPU gives elasticity and flexibility to allow adaptive motion and better grasping, while the CPLA gives rigidity to the structure and allows the actuator to be activated by a direct current (DC) power supply. Gripping is achieved by activating the actuator using a DC power supply with a power of 36 mW to generate Joule heating that increases the temperature of the actuator from room temperature to 85°C. Three different ratios of active-to-passive layers of the actuator were used, including 25%, 50%, and 75%. Maximum performance is achieved when the ratio is set to 50%, causing the actuator to bend by 58.90° and the gripping distance to reach 6.38 mm, which is 53.20% of the original distance before activation. The results show that the proposed gripper can perform gripping tasks while its fingers are at room temperature, demonstrating that it is suitable for handling temperature-sensitive objects in areas like soft robotic and surgical tools.

articleTitle: 5G Slicing with Machine Learning: Dataset Design, Model Adjustment and Performance Metrics
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The rapid expansion of 5G networks has opened up transformative opportunities in enabling diverse applications such as augmented reality, immersive simulations, and real-time collaborative tools. Central to maximizing these opportunities is the concept of network slicing, a technique that partitions a single 5G network into multiple slices tailored to meet specific service requirements. However, the dynamic nature of these applications and varying network demands poses significant challenges in effectively managing these slices. This paper focuses on integrating machine learning (ML) techniques to optimize network slicing for a variety of use cases. A comprehensive dataset design is proposed, capturing use cases, such as high-throughput content streaming and latency-sensitive real-time applications. Additionally, the paper emphasizes ML model fine-tuning and hyperparameter optimization to ensure efficient resource allocation and enhanced quality of service. Performance metrics include model accuracy, responsiveness, and scalability, critical for real-time and latency-sensitive scenarios. Gradient Boosting Trees (GBT) emerged as the best-performing classifier, consistently achieving superior accuracy and scalability among the nine classifiers tested. This study provides a framework for incorporating ML-driven network slicing, demonstrating its potential to optimize resource allocation and ensure high-quality performance for diverse 5G applications.

articleTitle: Vertical Beam Segmentation in Mobile Slit Lamp Images for Peripheral Anterior Chamber Angle Measurement
publicationTitle: 2025 21st IEEE International Colloquium on Signal Processing & Its Applications (CSPA)
abstract: The accurate segmentation of anterior chamber illumination in slit lamp images is crucial for calculating the anterior chamber angle (ACA), a vital parameter in diagnosing glaucoma and other anterior segment disorders. However, segmentation is complicated by challenges such as specular reflections, non-uniform illumination, and inconsistent image quality. This study evaluates and compares the performance of conventional image processing methods, specifically Otsu’ s multi-thresholding, and a deep learning-based UN et architecture for semantic segmentation. A robust preprocessing pipeline was developed to address artifacts and enhance vertical beam segmentation accuracy for peripheral ACA measurement on mobile slit lamp images. Experimental results demonstrate that Otsu's multi-thresholding achieves more refined vertical beam with a sensitivity of 0.8565, IoU of 0.6260, and DSC of 0.7603, outperforming the UNet-based approach (sensitivity: 0.8161, IoU: 0.5432, DSC: 0.6915). This finding highlights the advantages and limitations of both approaches, with optimized preprocessing playing a key role in improving ACA measurement. This research provides insights into the practical integration of segmentation techniques into clinical workflows, bridging the gap between advanced computational methods and their real-world application in ophthalmology.
